question: What do this decoder and three others do with a stream written past a bound of the format or into a field whose meaning is not public, and with three fields no real stream sets?
method: crates/oadec-synth gets a second list beside its recipes: probes, each a recipe with the rules `verify` finds it against. tools/synth_accept.py writes them with the recipes and runs FFmpeg, `truehdd` and Dolby's decoder on each as in evidence 10, comparing what each writes with the samples the stream was written from; it records what each did and asks no confirmation of a probe. `oadec verify --json` and `oadec decode -p 0 --format pcm` are run the same way. Before any stream was given a name, eighteen candidates were written with the same writer to see which the decoders read alike: those became recipes, the rest probes. Five mutations of how the decoder reads these fields (tools/mutants.py) were run against the suite of the commit this branch starts from, against the suite of this branch, and against the tests over the written streams alone, every test run to its end.

reading: Three of the fields no real stream sets turn out to have one meaning that two outside decoders or more agree on, and the streams that set them are recipes now. An output shift below nought is a shift to the right: truehdd and Dolby's decoder give the samples, as this decoder does, and FFmpeg's says it has not implemented it and shifts nothing. Guard bits are read alike by all four, sent again, cleared, given up, or sent with a restart header. The update of the heavy dynamic range control changes no sample; truehdd refuses the bit that announces it. The probes are the other kind, and what they show is where each decoder draws its lines. Dolby's decoder reads five blocks to a segment and a major sync in every unit, both past bounds its own description states, so the two rules that warn there are rightly no more than warnings. It refuses nine matrices, and so does FFmpeg's; this decoder and truehdd read them, and `verify` says nothing, which is a rule to write once the bound has been counted on real streams. And it refuses a protected block however the size is counted and whatever the check byte, so the one open question about that syntax stays open: FFmpeg takes the size to count its own field, truehdd and this decoder take it not to, and `block.data_bits` fails a stream on a reading no measurement here confirms. No real stream sets `error_protect`, so the rule has never fired. Of 5 mutations of how these fields are read, 3 passed the suite before and 2 more were caught by one hand-built unit test alone; with the streams all are caught, every one by the tests over the streams alone.
